title: Operator-approved compute budget: $10 project, $5 per-job hard cap (adjustable), enforced by the quote gate
summary: Operator approval in chat on 2026-09-29: "I would like to approve a budget of 10$ for now and a per job hard cap of 5, with the option to set that to something else later." budget.py stores machine-wide operator policy in ~/.agent-os/budget.json (shared by every checkout, outside Git), appends every change to budget-history.jsonl, and keeps an append-only spend ledger (actual / reserved / release). `orchestrate budget show|set` exposes it; set is an operator action (policy approval_required_for spending_limit_change) and autonomous agents never raise it. quote.py gates each paid option on the effective budget (budget.effective): approved only when the machine budget is approved; job cap = min(machine cap, workload cap); project limit = min(remaining machine budget after recorded spend, workload project limit), so workloads can only tighten. The budget was set to project_usd 10, job_hard_cap_usd 5 on this machine. Consequence check: the EVR-0017 example batch (high estimate $7.70 on the cheapest A100) is now correctly blocked by the $5 cap. The approval covers spend within these caps; provisioning code does not exist yet and the stored RunPod key is read-only, and the first real launch will still be confirmed with the operator.
